title: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
context_label: Previously treated unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
therapy_label: Antibody–drug conjugate · days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks
schedule_summary: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.
purpose: To control the cancer, relieve or delay symptoms, and help people live longer. This advanced-disease regimen does not promise a cure or an individual duration of benefit.
indication_text: NCCP00794a covers adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease. The NCCP entry specifies ECOG 0–1. Broader European licensed indications must be checked separately against the applicable Irish regimen and reimbursement pathway.
administration_text: The first infusion takes about three hours; later infusions usually take one to two hours if the earlier infusion was tolerated. Premedicines, checks and at least 30 minutes of observation after every infusion add to the visit. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.
monitoring_summary: Before the first treatment: full blood count, kidney and liver blood tests, glucose and electrolytes including magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Pregnancy testing is needed where relevant. ECG is added if clinically indicated. The team checks infection, medicines, previous low blood counts and whether preventive G-CSF injections are appropriate. Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle; the neutrophil count must also meet the separate Day 8 threshold before that infusion. Glucose and the listed electrolytes are checked every second cycle. Pregnancy testing is repeated before each cycle where relevant. Review diarrhoea, hydration, nausea, oral intake, fever and infection before each infusion. Scans follow the individual response-assessment plan.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
agents.mechanism: Carries the topoisomerase-I inhibitor SN-38 using an antibody that recognises Trop-2
agents.explanation: The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. Its linked SN-38 payload interferes with topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in managing DNA during copying, which can damage dividing cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected, particularly blood-forming cells and the gut; being antibody-directed does not mean it is free of chemotherapy-type effects.
agents.watch: The most important early problems to act on are fever or infection with low neutrophils, diarrhoea and dehydration, persistent nausea/vomiting, and infusion reactions. Report symptoms early rather than waiting for a planned scan or clinic.
risks: Low neutrophils and serious infection, including febrile neutropenia
Diarrhoea, dehydration and electrolyte loss; sometimes kidney injury
Infusion reactions, including rare life-threatening reactions
Potential harm to an unborn baby and effects on fertility

anatomy: Fever, shivering or suddenly feeling unwell needs immediate oncology advice; a low neutrophil count itself may cause no symptoms.
Report loose stools early, especially with cramps, fever, dizziness or reduced urine. Follow the prescribed diarrhoea plan.
Use preventive medicines for both infusion days. Contact the team if you cannot keep fluids down.
Tell the team about limiting tiredness, breathlessness or dizziness; blood tests help identify anaemia and other causes.
Hair thinning or loss can occur; ask about practical scalp and appearance support.
Tell staff immediately about rash, swelling, breathing difficulty or faintness during treatment.
anatomy_note: Selected effects specific to these medicines. This is not a prediction of which symptoms you will experience.

monitoring_schedule.note: Reference timing, not booked appointments. Ask who requests each test, when it is due, who reviews the result and whom to contact if it is missing. Delays can change cycle numbers; time-based monitoring remains time-based.

urgent_extra: Contact the oncology service immediately for fever, shivering or feeling acutely unwell; significant diarrhoea, inability to keep fluids down, dizziness, very little urine, or abdominal pain. Do not wait for the next treatment visit. During an infusion, tell staff immediately about breathing difficulty, swelling, rash, chest discomfort or faintness. Use the emergency service for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or other life-threatening symptoms.

sections.title: Plan two visits per cycle
sections.text: Day 1 and Day 8 are treatment days. Allow time for blood review, premedicines, the infusion and at least 30 minutes of observation afterwards. The first infusion is longer than later ones.

sections.title: Cannula or existing venous access
sections.text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access. A port is not automatically required and this regimen has no take-home pump. If you already have a port, staff access and flush it according to local policy; report pain, redness or swelling.

sections.title: Before leaving the unit
sections.text: Confirm the Day 8 appointment, blood-test arrangements, nausea medicines, written diarrhoea instructions and the number to call if unwell. If G-CSF is prescribed, ask exactly which days to take it around both treatment visits.

sections.title: If treatment is delayed
sections.text: A low count or significant side effect can mean a delay or dose change. The team will give the revised plan; do not calculate a replacement infusion from this diagram.

sections.title: If radiotherapy is also planned
sections.text: Radiotherapy is not an automatic phase of this advanced-disease regimen. If needed for local symptoms or another reason, the oncology and radiotherapy teams agree its timing and any treatment interruption.

evidence.title: ASCENT evidence in previously treated triple-negative breast cancer
evidence.population: ASCENT studied people with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after previous treatment.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in the population without baseline brain metastases.
evidence.interpretation: Sacituzumab delayed cancer growth and improved survival in the trial. The main early analysis and the later full-study analysis used different patient groups, so their results are described separately in the clinical evidence. Your benefit and side effects may differ from the study averages.
evidence.limitations: The primary analysis excluded baseline brain metastases; the overall-population estimates differ. Open-label design, selected trial fitness and previous-treatment requirements limit extrapolation. Group medians do not predict an individual patient's benefit. This trial does not establish eligibility for every broader current EU indication.
evidence.intro: This explains the study setting and its meaning. Ask the team how the evidence applies to you.
evidence.comparison_label: One of several standard single chemotherapy medicines.

teachback: Which medicine is taken or given when, what checks are expected next, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Blood-count rules differ between Day 1 and Day 8. Known reduced UGT1A1 activity may increase side effects, but routine genotype testing is not required by the EU product information. Important differences between the NCCP and current EU dose-modification wording are flagged for Consultant and oncology-pharmacy review; patients should never change the dose themselves. Discuss fertility before treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for six months after the final dose for women who could become pregnant, and for three months for male patients with female partners who could become pregnant. Do not breastfeed during treatment; the EU product information also advises against breastfeeding for one month after the last dose.

support.title: Prevent nausea before both doses
support.text: This is a high-emetic-risk regimen. Preventive antiemetics are needed for both Day 1 and Day 8, with take-home medicines and clear instructions. The steroid used as an infusion premedicine also provides antiemetic cover, so the team must reconcile the total dose.

support.title: A written diarrhoea plan
support.text: Report diarrhoea early. The team assesses infection, dehydration and electrolyte loss, and supplies an appropriate antidiarrhoeal prescription. Follow the written oncology instructions; do not improvise repeated high doses of loperamide.

support.title: Blood-count support
support.text: G-CSF injections may be considered from cycle 1 if the risk of febrile neutropenia is increased, or after significant neutropenia. Product and timing depend on the two-infusion schedule and the prescribing plan.

support.title: Infusion-reaction prevention
support.text: The unit gives premedicines to reduce reaction risk and observes you during and after each infusion. Tell staff immediately if you feel different or unwell.

support.title: Early cramping or diarrhoea during an infusion
support.text: This can be an acute cholinergic effect and needs staff assessment. Atropine may be used for later infusions when appropriate; tell the team if you have glaucoma.

timeline.label: Day 1 infusion
timeline.text: Blood review, premedicines, infusion and observation

timeline.label: Day 8 infusion
timeline.text: Reassess symptoms and ANC, then premedicines, infusion and observation

timeline.label: Nausea / bowel symptoms
timeline.text: May occur after either dose or between visits. This is a watch window, not a predicted symptom period.

timeline.label: Blood-count / infection watch
timeline.text: Risk varies across the cycle; fever or feeling unwell needs urgent advice on any day.

timeline.label: Energy / recovery
timeline.text: Fatigue may fluctuate or build over repeated cycles. No planned infusion on Day 15 does not guarantee absence of side effects.

timeline_note: Treatment days are specified by the regimen. Symptom timing varies; the full-cycle symptom bands show that an effect can occur at any point, not a measured probability or severity.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment and rest
chronology_notes.text: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.

chronology_notes.title: Tests and appointments
chronology_notes.text: Use the monitoring table for baseline and later checks. A rest week does not remove infection or other risks.

safety_note: Contact the oncology service immediately for fever, shivering or feeling acutely unwell; significant diarrhoea, inability to keep fluids down, dizziness, very little urine, or abdominal pain. chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: To control the cancer, relieve or delay symptoms, and help people live longer. This advanced-disease regimen does not promise a cure or an individual duration of benefit.

items.title: Who this covers
items.text: NCCP00794a covers adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease. The NCCP entry specifies ECOG 0–1. Broader European licensed indications must be checked separately against the applicable Irish regimen and reimbursement pathway.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: 10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; prescribed reductions may apply. The first infusion takes about three hours; later infusions usually take one to two hours if the earlier infusion was tolerated. Premedicines, checks and at least 30 minutes of observation after every infusion add to the visit. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.

items.title: Duration and decisions
items.text: Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable. There is no fixed number of cycles; the oncology team reviews benefit, scans and tolerability.

items.title: Individual safety and source differences
items.text: Blood-count rules differ between Day 1 and Day 8. Known reduced UGT1A1 activity may increase side effects, but routine genotype testing is not required by the EU product information. Important differences between the NCCP and current EU dose-modification wording are flagged for Consultant and oncology-pharmacy review; patients should never change the dose themselves.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Blood tests assess treatment safety. Scans assess disease or investigate symptoms. Echo and ECG answer different questions.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Before the first treatment: full blood count, kidney and liver blood tests, glucose and electrolytes including magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Pregnancy testing is needed where relevant. ECG is added if clinically indicated. The team checks infection, medicines, previous low blood counts and whether preventive G-CSF injections are appropriate.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle; the neutrophil count must also meet the separate Day 8 threshold before that infusion. Glucose and the listed electrolytes are checked every second cycle. Pregnancy testing is repeated before each cycle where relevant. Review diarrhoea, hydration, nausea, oral intake, fever and infection before each infusion. Scans follow the individual response-assessment plan.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: An ECG is used when clinically indicated. Sacituzumab alone does not require a routine echocardiogram schedule. Cardiac symptoms or other medicines may change the plan.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: A routine DXA scan is not a sacituzumab-specific requirement. Bone health, bone metastases and any bone-strengthening treatment need their own individual plan.

chapters.title: Your wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Additional treatments depend on the confirmed setting and indication.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: If informative, particularly when elevated at baseline or disease is not readily measurable, tumour markers may supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker rise alone should not trigger a treatment change. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
items.text: Discuss fertility before treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for six months after the final dose for women who could become pregnant, and for three months for male patients with female partners who could become pregnant. Do not breastfeed during treatment; the EU product information also advises against breastfeeding for one month after the last dose.
